title: Vectors
confusion: ❌ 'The triangle law and parallelogram law give different resultants.' ✅ They are mathematically EQUIVALENT — the triangle is half the parallelogram, so the same diagonal/resultant appears in both.
❌ 'θ is the angle between the two sides inside the parallelogram.' ✅ θ is the angle between the vectors placed TAIL-TO-TAIL at the common origin.
❌ 'A dot product results in a vector.' ✅ Dot product (scalar product) *always* results in a SCALAR quantity (e.g., Work).
❌ 'A cross product direction is arbitrary.' ✅ Direction is strictly defined by the Right-Hand Rule (RHR), perpendicular to the plane of the two vectors.
notes: **Scalar:** magnitude only (mass, speed, work, temperature). **Vector:** magnitude + direction (displacement, velocity, force, momentum).
**Triangle law / Parallelogram law:** resultant R of two vectors P and Q inclined at angle θ: R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ, tan α = Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ).
**Resolution:** a vector can be split into components along chosen axes: A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ.
**Scalar (dot) product:** A·B = AB cos θ = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z. Work is a dot product. Vectors perpendicular ⇒ dot product = 0.
**Vector (cross) product:** A×B = AB sin θ (direction by right-hand rule). Torque and angular momentum are cross products. Parallel vectors ⇒ cross product = 0.
